title: feat(wire): a tangent arc lead-in and lead-out
body:
## What changed

Wire Contour has an opt-in tangent arc lead-in and lead-out. The straight lead stays the default.

- **Parameter.** `WireContourOp.lead_arc_radius: Option<f64>` (mm). `None` is the straight lead. The project file writes `lead_arc_radius` only when it is set (serde default), so old files read the straight lead and do not change.
- **MCP.** `edit_operation` takes `lead_arc_radius` (a number, or `null` for the straight lead). `list_operation_types { "kind": "wire_contour" }` lists it. The `camcraft-mcp` skill row names the field and its refusals.
- **UI.** The Geometry tab has a "Tangent arc lead-in and lead-out" check and a "Lead arc radius" row. The check seeds 0.5 mm. Apply uses the existing undoable `EditOperationParams`.
- **Motion.** A new module `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/arc_lead.rs` builds the leads. `wire_contour_arcs_led(chain, p, lead)` takes the lead. `wire_contour_arcs` keeps its signature and the straight lead. `arc_cut.rs` changes only in the lead code of `wire_contour_arcs`; `stitch` does not change. The branch merges `origin/main` with PR #3988; the one conflict was in the test helpers of `wire_dxf_selection/arcs.rs`, and both sides are kept.

## The lead geometry

- The seam stays the path's nearest point to the start hole (the #3937 rule, with the +X rule for a hole at the centre of a circle).
- The lead circle has the stated radius. It touches the path at the seam, with its centre on the waste side: left of the walk for a die, right for a punch.
- Lead-in: a straight from the hole to the point where the tangent from the hole touches the lead circle, then an arc on the circle to the seam. The wire meets the path in the path's own direction.
- Lead-out: the mirror. The wire continues on the lead circle at the end of the lap, then goes back to the hole on a tangent straight.
- The two leads close a small waste piece between them. The path note says so. The wire verdict counts it as a second freed piece, and the capture statement covers it (a selected DXF cut needs that statement).
- The author confirmed this lead-out design: a tangent lead-in and a tangent lead-out, the small extra waste piece stated in a path note, and two freed pieces under the capture statement. A lead-out back along the lead-in arc was not chosen, because the wire would turn 180 degrees at the entry point.

## The radius rule and the refusals

The stated radius is never changed, and the cut never falls back to the straight lead silently. Each refusal is by name:

- A radius that is not larger than the kerf offset (wire radius + spark gap). The command door refuses it when the operation is made, edited or given a new tool, after the condition resolves: `wire_sketch_arcs::lead_arc_radius_refusal`, called from `wire_gate`. The create, edit, retool and MCP paths all go through that gate. The generator keeps its own check for a loaded file or a machine whose condition changed later.
- A start hole that is not outside the lead circle. On the normal through the seam, the hole must be more than twice the radius from the path.
- A lead span nearer the profile than the kerf offset (an arc that crosses the profile or the waste-side clearance). With the nearest-point seam, a generated lead stays in the disc about the hole that the path only touches. Thus this check is a guard. Its unit test reads it on a seam that is not the nearest point.
- At the command door and at generation: the arc lead with an open run, a 4-axis cut, a no-core burnout, tabs, skims, a taper, or an exit pick.
- At generation: the arc lead on a profile that is not a selected DXF chain (a model's section).

The lead circle's centre is written on the CL lattice (1e-6 mm). The arc radius is then the distance from that centre to the seam. Thus the arc ends on the seam exactly and is tangent there within the lattice.

## Alignment with the start and exit points (#3332, #1448)

The lead uses the start pick in `picks` as its hole. It adds no second notion of where the wire enters or leaves. The lead shape is an operation parameter beside the picks, as #1448 describes ("leads in at that point"). The exit pick of #3332 keeps its straight lead-out. The analytic route already refuses an exit pick, so the arc lead with an exit pick is refused by name. A later change can give the exit's lead-out the same arc.

## Posts

No post changes. The leads are line and arc moves, so the generic ISO, Sodick and G-EDM posts write the lead arcs as G2/G3 (G03 on Sodick) with I/J. The first cut move is the tangent straight from the hole, so the Sodick rule (no arc as the first cut move) holds.

## Readings

Die circle, radius 5, hole at its centre, radius 1 lead (`wire-iso/wire_dxf_die_circle_arc_lead.nc`):

```
G0 X6. Y5.
G1 X9.574 Y4.035
G3 X10.835 Y5. I0.261 J0.965
G3 X1.165 Y5. I-4.835 J0.
G3 X10.835 Y5. I4.835 J0.
G3 X9.574 Y5.965 I-1. J0.
G1 X6. Y5.
```

The lead arc centre is X9.835 Y5. (radius 1, on the waste side of the entry X10.835 Y5.). The entry point is the same as with the straight lead.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/arc_lead_tests.rs` (motion lib):
  - `a_die_circle_is_entered_and_left_on_tangent_arcs`
  - `a_line_and_arc_punch_is_entered_and_left_on_tangent_arcs`
  - `a_hole_too_near_for_the_lead_circle_is_refused_by_name`
  - `a_radius_not_over_the_kerf_offset_is_refused_by_name`
  - `a_lead_that_would_cross_the_profile_is_refused_by_name`
  - `a_lead_arc_moved_two_microns_into_the_product_is_caught_by_the_kerf_law` (the mutation)
  - `the_straight_lead_is_the_default_and_unchanged`
- `crates/app/tests/wire_dxf_selection/arc_lead.rs` (in the existing `wire_dxf_selection` suite):
  - `die_circle_with_an_arc_lead_is_tangent_verified_and_posts_its_goldens` (ISO, Sodick, G-EDM)
  - `line_and_arc_punch_and_a_polygon_take_the_arc_lead_and_pass_the_verdict`
  - `a_hole_too_near_and_a_pair_the_arc_lead_is_not_cut_with_are_refused_by_name`
  - `a_radius_at_or_under_the_kerf_offset_is_refused_at_the_command_door` (review finding 1: a radius equal to the C110 offset of 0.165 mm and a radius of 0.1 mm; the edit and the create are refused; the operation and the undo history do not change; a radius 0.001 mm over the offset passes)
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_wire_contour/arc_lead.rs` (in the existing `mcp_wire_contour` suite): `edit_operation_sets_the_arc_lead_radius_and_refuses_what_it_is_not_cut_with` (MCP round trip, door refusal, a radius of 0.1 mm refused at the door with the operation unchanged and no undo step, model refusal, undo).
- `crates/app/src/project/wire_edm_dto.rs`: `the_arc_lead_radius_round_trips_and_is_absent_for_the_straight_lead` (project file).
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wire_page_tests.rs`: `wire_tangent_arc_lead_toggle_applies_and_undoes`.
- `list_operation_types_and_skill_match_wire_contour_dto_and_tool_law` now also pins the new field in the DTO, the MCP listing and the skill.

## Goldens

- New: `wire-iso/wire_dxf_die_circle_arc_lead.nc`, `sodick-wire/wire_dxf_die_circle_arc_lead.nc`, `g-edm/wire_dxf_die_circle_arc_lead.nc`, `wire-iso/wire_dxf_punch_fillet_arc_lead.nc`.
- Moved: none. The straight-lead goldens do not change (`wire_dxf_selection` and the wire post suites pass unchanged).

## Not exercised

- The arc lead on a model's polygon profile: refused by name (see the decision file).
- The arc lead with an exit pick, skims, tabs, a taper, a burnout or a 4-axis cut: refused by name.
- No control ran the posted programs.

## Other notes

- New directory-suite files only (`wire_dxf_selection/arc_lead.rs`, `mcp_wire_contour/arc_lead.rs`); no new top-level test binary.
- Each `WireContourOp` struct literal in the app tests gets `lead_arc_radius: None` (mechanical).
- Helpers in `crates/app/tests/wire_dxf_selection/arcs.rs` are now `pub(super)`, so the new submodule uses them.
- The decision file is `docs/decisions/3991-wire-arc-lead.md`.
- The merge of `origin/main` at `baad348f1` (with #4003) had one conflict in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wire_page_tests.rs`. Each side added tests at the end of the file, and both sides are kept. Main also added a `WireContourOp` literal in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/agie_inspection_tests.rs`; it gets `lead_arc_radius: None`.
- The shared check is in `wire_sketch_arcs.rs` (176 lines). `crates/app/src/mcp/job.rs` and `crates/app/src/operation/wire_op.rs` do not grow in this fix.

## Screenshots

The Wire page, Geometry tab, synthetic wire ISO fixture machine, condition C110, page harness 620 x 1400, on head `1253641ee`. The images are on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch, not on this branch.

| Tangent arc lead off (the default) | Tangent arc lead on, with the radius row |
|---|---|
| ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-4002/before-wire-page-tangent-lead-off.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/pr-4002/after-wire-page-tangent-lead-on.png) |

## Gate

All on the final head `1253641ee0b7c7a3327c6d8e0a9496003c7e5461` (merge of `origin/main` at `baad348f1`, then the review fixes):

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 772 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (77.5 min). The plan includes `motion suites: lib`, `ui suites: lib`, `wire_dxf_selection`, `mcp_wire_contour`, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` and `first_part_programs`.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (8.4 min).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The new test `a_radius_at_or_under_the_kerf_offset_is_refused_at_the_command_door` was red before the fix ("edit refused" panic) and green after it.
- No heavy step: this is a `P6` PR ("Heavy lanes at review").

Changelog: Wire Contour: a tangent arc lead-in and lead-out (`lead_arc_radius`, mm) for a selected DXF profile, next to the straight lead; a lead that does not fit is refused by name.

Process change: yes (`.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`: the Wire Contour row names `lead_arc_radius`).

Effort: high
